reviews.evidence: The core defines an abstract finite root system in an inner-product space. Weyl groups, Cartan subalgebras, Killing forms, and classification are Lie-theoretic applications or context, so they are not prerequisites for this generic definition.

The definition is a subalgebra that is nilpotent and self-normalizing. The Lie-subalgebra concept is therefore a direct prerequisite; semisimple and nilpotent structure remain relevant to the stated refinements.

The decomposition requires a semisimple Lie algebra, Cartan subalgebra, adjoint action, root spaces, and the Killing-form pairing used in the stated root-system consequence. Positive roots, Dynkin diagrams, and the abstract root-system knowl are consequences or later organization, not prerequisites for the decomposition.

The opening definition acts on the dual of a finite-dimensional group representation, so group-representation and vector-space concepts are direct prerequisites. Smooth and Hilbert dual variants remain later qualifications.

The definition takes a crystallographic root system and simple roots, and its relation to the weight lattice is stated directly. Simply connectedness appears only in a later group-level application and is not a prerequisite for the root lattice.

The root-space definition uses a Cartan subalgebra and a root of the Lie algebra. The sl2 example illustrates the definition later and does not define the general eigenspace, so it is not a prerequisite.

The source defines an abelian Lie algebra from the ambient Lie algebra and its bracket; both listed prerequisites are direct ingredients, while equivalent characterizations and applications remain later context.
The core definition is commutativity of a Lie group, requiring only the ambient Lie-group structure; commutator and Lie-algebra characterizations are later context.

The adjoint action starts from conjugation in a Lie group and differentiates at the identity, so the listed Lie-group and Lie-algebra prerequisites match the construction; exponential and root-theory references are applications.
The theorem explicitly assumes connectedness and identifies the kernel of the adjoint action with the group center; all three listed prerequisites are used in the statement and proof context.
The adjoint representation is defined by the Lie bracket on a Lie algebra and its homomorphism property uses the Jacobi identity; the two listed prerequisites are direct.

Admissibility is defined for a representation of a real reductive group relative to a maximal compact subgroup, with finite multiplicities of K-types; the listed ambient and K-finiteness concepts are the needed ingredients.

Ado’s theorem states an injective Lie-algebra homomorphism into a general linear Lie algebra, so Lie algebra, homomorphism, subalgebra, general-linear algebra, and injectivity are all direct statement ingredients.

The definition uses a Lie-group orbit map for a strongly continuous unitary representation and compares analytic vectors with derived smooth vectors; the four listed prerequisites directly support those notions.
BCH is stated for a Lie group and exponential map using iterated Lie brackets, with nilpotence as the truncation hypothesis; each listed prerequisite is used directly.
Bi-invariance is defined by invariance under left and right translations; the listed Lie-group and translation concepts are exactly the operations in the definition.
The metric is defined by invariance under left and right translations, and its Lie-algebra formulation uses the adjoint action; the four listed prerequisites match those claims.

The source is a Borel–de Siebenthal structural theorem for connected compact groups, using root systems, maximal tori, Dynkin diagrams, and central quotients; each listed prerequisite occurs in the theorem’s setup or conclusion.

The branching statement compares group and Lie-algebra representations under restriction and tracks irreducible multiplicities; all six listed representation, restriction, multiplicity, and ambient Lie concepts are used.

The decomposition is formed from the ±1 eigenspaces of a Cartan involution on a real reductive Lie algebra; automorphism, subalgebra, and inner-product prerequisites support the displayed bracket and orthogonality properties.

The Cartan involution definition is for the Lie algebra of a real reductive group and uses an invariant bilinear form, Lie-algebra automorphism, Killing form, and reductive structure; the listed prerequisites are all explicit setup ingredients.
The Cartan matrix is formed from simple roots in the root system of a semisimple Lie algebra and displayed as a matrix using an inner product; the six listed prerequisites provide these ingredients.

The proof explicitly expands an element using the root-space decomposition and tests normalization of a Cartan subalgebra; semisimplicity, Cartan structure, and root-space decomposition are therefore direct prerequisites.
Cartan’s criterion compares semisimplicity with nondegeneracy of the Killing form for a Lie algebra; the three listed concepts are exactly the theorem’s ambient object and alternatives.

The solvability criterion is stated through the derived series, derived subalgebra, and Killing form, with Cartan’s semisimplicity criterion used in the surrounding argument; the listed prerequisites match those ingredients.

The Casimir construction uses the Killing form and a basis of a semisimple Lie algebra to produce an element of its universal enveloping algebra and an operator; the listed prerequisites cover each construction.

The theorem embeds irreducible admissible representations of a real reductive group into normalized principal series and uses maximal compact and Harish–Chandra data; the listed prerequisites are the theorem’s stated categories.

The globalization theorem relates Harish–Chandra modules to Casselman–Wallach representations for real reductive groups via an equivalence of categories; every listed prerequisite appears in that assertion.

The definition combines a real reductive group, maximal compact subgroup, smooth Fréchet representation, K-finite Harish–Chandra module, and moderate-growth seminorm bounds; all listed prerequisites are explicit conditions.
The source derives the Möbius action from the proper Lorentz-group and celestial-sphere identifications; those two concepts are the only prerequisites for its opening claim.
The center is defined by the Lie bracket and then identified as a subalgebra, ideal, and kernel of the adjoint representation; the listed prerequisites support each basic property presented.
The group center is defined inside a Lie group and its later properties invoke normal subgroups, conjugation, and the adjoint action; the listed prerequisites follow those explicit claims.
The source defines the center of the universal enveloping algebra for a Lie algebra over a field; the three listed prerequisites are explicit ambient constructions in the definition.
The quotient construction assumes a Lie group and a closed central subgroup, then invokes the quotient group and coset-space structures; all four listed prerequisites are used in the core.
The centralizer is defined for a Lie subalgebra by the bracket-commutation condition; the sole listed prerequisite is therefore the exact ambient structure required.

The theorem assumes a root-space decomposition in its opening hypotheses, so that theorem is a direct prerequisite alongside semisimplicity, a Cartan subalgebra, regularity, and the centralizer operation.

Removing fiber-bundles/lie-group keeps the prerequisite core at Lie-algebra level while retaining semisimple Lie algebra, Lie subalgebra, Killing form, and Lie algebra.
Defines singular simplices, the alternating face boundary, and verifies the chain-complex structure; these are the complete prerequisites for singular chains.
Defines H_n as cycles modulo boundaries of the singular chain complex and records functoriality; the chain-complex and homology abstractions are genuine prerequisites.

The opening definition uses H_n(M;R), and the boundary variant uses relative homology; both now point to complete singular homology foundations. Integration removed trailing whitespace only.
